column1: # Game profile of Boomerang Fu (Switch, update 1.3.7 = v1441792, with the two licence-only DLC). Plays on the Mac
# Unity 2022.3.54f1 (IL2CPP) with FMOD, SDK 18.3.5: the sdk and the movie module (subsdk0) are Monster Train 2's builds (Super Mario Galaxy's sdk), whose node area cut is already in
# dm/tools/sdk_patches.py. The game shows no movie. The provisional profile was right as generated; it needed no host change
# Local multiplayer, controller only: left stick moves, A slashes, B dashes, X throws; one player plays against bots

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie, which main imports from)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup hands application pool − used memory to StandardAllocator as virtual address memory
# and never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. Monster Train 2's layout (the heap check's 1 GB pool, the 5 GB block). Measured on the Mac over 10 minutes of matches: about 1.0 GB mapped, the
# alias region's high-water mark +4.27 GB of 4.375 GB (the SDK's AddressRegionManager places a new region in the highest free gap first, so the mark climbs while freed gaps below
# are reused once the top is full; play went on for 6 more minutes there), 1.6 GB resident and 1.2 GB of Metal allocations, flat
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# everything is under Data/: the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets files
